hook: Saltier mid-depth water offsets 58% of thermal sea level rise in the southwest Indian Ocean.

readout.label: Mid-depth thermal expansion offset by salinity

summary: Water expands as it warms but contracts as it gets saltier. Using 2004-2023 Argo float data, the authors split trends into layer shifts and changes along constant density, and found the mid-depth salinity trend is almost entirely along-density change. The temperature split is weakly constrained, and the result does not prove the cause is salinification of one water mass.
title: Intermediate Water Salinification Counteracts Thermosteric Sea‐Level Rise in the Tropical Southwest Indian Ocean
